To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) bears selectively kill salmon that have spent the least time on the spawning grounds (highest energy) when they forage in environments that facilitate choice; (2) bears are less selective at environments that are more difficult to forage in (i.e. where capture success is less than encounter rates); and (3) the energetic value of salmon is a major factor influencing bear predation rates at streams where bears are the dominant salmon predator.
